purpose: §18: executed proof, real Postgres, before any recovery resumption.
procedure: Provisioned TEST_A/TEST_B/TEST_C as three real, separate Postgres databases (createdb + prisma migrate deploy each) on the same server as the persistent regression database.
Seeded each with a distinctly-named, id-unique company (iso-test-a-company / -b- / -c-).
Confirmed each ephemeral database's own current_database() matches the disposable naming convention, and that the REAL persistent `headroom` database is correctly REJECTED by the same check.
Ran a destructive `company.deleteMany({})` reset against TEST_A ONLY, gated by assertDisposableDatabase(clientA) immediately before it (the same call pattern any real reset helper must use).

Verified: TEST_A's company count is 0; TEST_B's and TEST_C's companies are untouched; the persistent database's own company set (coherent, matthews, fixture-fwrg-2021-credit-agreement-co) is unchanged and does NOT contain the TEST_A company.
Confirmed a naive `assertDisposableDatabase(persistent)` call against the real database throws before any destructive statement could run.
Destroyed TEST_A/TEST_B/TEST_C (dropdb --if-exists --force each) in the test's own afterAll.
result: npx vitest run tests/infrastructure/db-isolation-adversarial.test.ts -> 1 file, 4 tests, ALL PASSING.

postTestVerification.leftoverEphemeralDatabases: NONE (psql -l shows zero headroom_test_* databases after the run)
postTestVerification.persistentDatabaseCompanySet: ['fixture-fwrg-2021-credit-agreement-co', 'coherent', 'matthews'] - identical to before the adversarial test ran; byte-for-byte unaffected by three real database creations, a real seed, and a real destructive reset happening elsewhere on the same server.

conclusion: Isolation is demonstrated, not merely designed. Per §18's own explicit instruction ('If this cannot be demonstrated: STOP'), this clears the gate to proceed to package recovery (§19-26).
